standout_why: Compared against theofficejournal.com (under-$150 page), dejaflow.com and twelvetabs.com; deskfinds.com returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The Office Journal page lists four single 14 to 15.6-inch extenders with almost no current prices and one weight (Miesebe 1.87 lb). Dejaflow lists ten prices dated 2026-02-16 with no weights or wattages, and already includes one two-screen set under $150 (AOKER-P5, 2 × 15.6-inch, $139.00 in February), which is why this is not a 3. Twelvetabs gives prices and two weights. As far as I could tell through page summaries (which did their own arithmetic on request), none of the three prints a per-screen cost, an added-area figure, a per-square-inch cost or a battery-drain figure.
decides: It splits the pick by laptop. Where the laptop can drive two external displays, the FOPO S1 wins the question: two added screens and 1.61 times the added area of a single 15.6-inch screen at about the same price. On a base M1/M2 MacBook (Apple states one external display for the M2 Air), a driver-free two-screen extender extends one screen only, by Apple's limit; I did not confirm how the S1's second screen behaves there. That makes the S1 $144 for one usable 14-inch screen (83.75 sq in), and a single 15.6-inch screen wins on area: the Mobile Pixels Fold at 104.0 sq in for $143.99, or the ASUS ZenScreen MB169CK at 103.3 sq in. The battery figure (a 7.64 W screen takes 14.5% of a 52.6 Wh battery per hour) applies to every bus-powered pick and doubles roughly for two screens.
